key_insight: AIPatient Arena shows that medical LLMs can sound strong in interviews and explanations, but still struggle with information coverage, ambiguity, and diagnostic reasoning in realistic multi-turn consultations.
clinical_relevance: Workflow-oriented evaluation using EHR-grounded patient context may better predict whether an LLM is ready for clinical consultation than final-answer scoring alone.
method: Built patient-specific knowledge graphs from EHR data
Scored models across 8 clinical competence dimensions
evidence_signal: The study evaluated models on a primary cohort of 437 patients plus two out-of-distribution cohorts of 119 and 67 patients, revealing strong QS/ET performance but weaker IC and Dx scores.
watch_item: The framework is still an evaluation tool, and stronger dialogue performance does not by itself guarantee safe real-world deployment or reliable treatment planning.
paper_title: AIPatient Arena: EHR-grounded evaluation of large language models in end-to-end clinical consultation workflows
